title: The Stag That Stopped
sceneText:
The stag comes into the afternoon light and stands in the clear ground between two oaks.

The best shot in the field already has it, and Baron Henk raises a hand.

He is keeping the chance back. Every year one stag is left for the most welcome guest, or for whoever the Baron thinks is worth a try.

Nobody is looking at the stag. They are watching Henk, or watching who Henk is watching.

Henk’s eyes come to rest on you, hold for a second, and move off. He has not decided.

Beside you, Marguerite says quietly:

“He is not looking for somebody to shoot a deer. He is looking for somebody to talk to.”

effects.logEntry: You stepped forward and took the stag.

choices.resultText:
You take one step forward.

Henk laughs at once, claps you hard on the back and holds out the gun. Somebody nearby says something and several of them laugh with him.

You raise it. The stag is still standing there, its head turned a little to one side, its ears moving.

From this distance it is larger than you had thought.

You did not fire. Or you did. The account stops here; whether that shot went home, nobody mentions again all day.

But you are talked to the whole afternoon. Somebody comes and asks where you are from. Somebody asks how long you mean to stay at Maplegate. Somebody tells you a story about last year’s stag, at length.

On the ride back at dusk you understand that Henk already has what he wanted.

He cleared a place, and then watched to see who would stand in it. You stood in it.

choices.text: Ask Marguerite quietly how Hartmann used to handle this moment

effects.logEntry: You quietly asked Marguerite how Hartmann used to handle this moment.

choices.resultText:
Her eyes do not leave the stag.

“He took half a step back,” she says. “Every year. Back behind somebody else, where Henk could not find him.”

“Seven years of stepping back?”

“Seven years,” she says. “The eighth he did not come.”

Ahead of you somebody steps forward, and somebody else takes the chance.

Only then does Marguerite turn her head to look at you.

“A person can keep out of the way of a thing for many years,” she says. “But keeping out of the way costs something, and what it costs runs out.”

choices.text: Stay where you are and do nothing

effects.logEntry: You stayed where you were and did not move.

choices.resultText:
You do not move.

Henk’s eyes rest on you once more, shorter this time than before, and go elsewhere.

Somebody else steps forward.

Things carry on. The noise comes back up, as though those few seconds had not happened.

Marguerite says nothing further.

For the rest of that day Henk does not look at you again. He is not cold about it either; at supper he pours you wine and says two things about the weather.

He simply does not look at you again.
